what_its_for: Voriconazole is an antifungal medicine used to treat serious fungal infections in the body, such as infections in the lungs, blood, or other organs. It is also used to prevent fungal infections in people with weakened immune systems.
how_to_take: Take voriconazole exactly as your doctor prescribes. The tablet and liquid forms are taken by mouth on an EMPTY STOMACH — at least 1 hour before eating or 2 hours after eating. If you are taking the liquid (suspension), shake the bottle well for about 10 seconds before each use. Use the measuring device provided — do not use a household spoon. Do not mix the liquid with other drinks or medicines. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your weight, the type of infection, and how you respond to treatment. A common adult starting dose is 400 mg twice daily on the first day (loading dose), then 200 mg twice daily after that. Children's doses are based on weight. Always take doses at the same times each day, about 12 hours apart. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, light, and moisture. Store the liquid (suspension) in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze the liquid. Throw away any unused liquid 14 days after mixing. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid going out in the sun without protection — voriconazole can make your skin much more sensitive to sunlight and increase your risk of sunburn and skin cancer with long-term use. Always wear sunscreen (SPF 50+), protective clothing, and sunglasses outdoors. Do NOT drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you experience blurred or changed vision, as this medicine can affect your eyesight. Tell your doctor about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, because voriconazole has many drug interactions — including with blood thinners, certain antibiotics, seizure medicines, and cholesterol medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: changes in vision such as blurring, seeing colors differently, or sensitivity to light; skin rash, blistering, peeling, or severe sunburn; yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain (signs of liver problems); irregular heartbeat or chest pain; hallucinations or confusion; unusual bleeding or bruising; signs of low blood sugar (shakiness, sweating, hunger, dizziness); or if your symptoms are not improving or are getting worse.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days, but it is very important to finish the full course of treatment even if you feel well. Fungal infections can take several weeks to fully clear up. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping too early can allow the infection to come back.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Voriconazole can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control while taking this medicine. BREASTFEEDING: It is not known if voriconazole passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. CHILDREN: This medicine can be used in children 2 years and older, with doses based on weight. KIDNEY DISEASE: If you have kidney problems, the IV (intravenous) form may not be safe for you, but tablets or liquid are usually okay. LIVER DISEASE: Your dose may need to be adjusted. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems. ELDERLY: Older adults may need closer monitoring for side effects.
